description: Tunable data for bandit gang generation (docs/js/bandit-gang-generator.js). No code lives here -- species/clothing pools, rank composition, and mastery/difficulty scaling are all data so gangs can be rebalanced without touching game.js. Corpse loot per rank now lives in docs/config/loot/loot-pools.json (pools bandit_grunt/bandit_flasker/bandit_lieutenant/bandit_captain), alongside every other drop table.

clothingPool._comment: Slots + item ids intersected against each rolled species' own docs/config/species/<id>.json allowedCosmetics/cosmeticWeights at generation time -- a species that doesn't whitelist an item here (e.g. mashtzarr and hats) just never rolls it, no per-species override needed here. Exception: banditExclusiveIds (see below) bypass that whitelist check entirely.
clothingPool._banditExclusiveComment: facewrap is deliberately left out of every species' allowedCosmetics so ordinary NPCs/players never randomly roll it -- it's meant to be found exclusively on bandits (and thus lootable from their corpses). Listing it here lets bandit rolls use it anyway, bypassing the normal per-species whitelist intersection.
clothingPool._dyeComment: Dye ids are constructed as `dye:CLOTH:<variant>_<hueFamily>` (see docs/config/scratchbones-config.js's catalog builder ~line 864-890, and appliedDyes samples in docs/config/npcs/hobunji-starter-npc-database.json) -- restricting variant to the mid/low-saturation set (60%/30% sat, darker brightness) gives the worn, mismatched look without needing the full runtime dye catalog. Each filled slot rolls its OWN variant+hue independently -- slots are never color-matched to each other.
clothingPool._fillComment: 4 slots x 0.5 = 2 average filled slots for a grunt, per design. Each slot is rolled independently; if a roll comes up with zero slots filled, one random slot is force-filled so every bandit wears at least one clothing item. On top of that, hat and hood are independently guaranteed: every bandit ends up wearing a fine_hood, a facewrap, or a headband -- if that first pass leaves both empty, one is force-filled from whichever the bandit's species/gender allows.

gangComposition._flaskerComment: One Flasker for every N regular bandits (grunts): floor(grunts / N), so a camp with fewer than N grunts has none. Reinforcements are drawn in proportion to the reserve left, so refills keep the same mix.

gruntVariants._comment: Rare grunt replacements. The Slagothim Beastmaster uses the Tletingan avatar/species data (Tletingans use Slagothim culture and names) and brings one deliberately weak Dabinggi-hound driven by the normal companion follow/fight cadence.

weaponMetalTierRangeByRank._comment: Actual rolled metal still controls weapon appearance and armor. Each two enemy danger tiers expand the available metal ceiling by one step (up to leaded bronze). Metal reinforcement grade rises at the same cadence, from I to IV, using the same multiplier as player weapons.

rangedWeaponChanceByRank._comment: Bandits that pass this roll keep their normal melee weapon and also receive a ranged-slot weapon.

culturalRangedWeightByRank._comment: After a bandit passes rangedWeaponChanceByRank, each trust-dialogue weapon that both belongs to that bandit's species and has a real ranged definition is added beside crossbow/scatterbow with this weight. This changes only the weapon mix, never the chance of receiving a ranged weapon.

masteryBaseByRank._comment: Added to floor(dangerTier / 2), capped at 5, so mastery and held ability power advance across eight danger tiers without maxing out halfway through.

heldAbilitiesByRank._comment: How many hold-family abilities (hold1/hold2 slots, see docs/js/combat/combat-loadout.js SLOT_CATEGORIES) this rank is given. Grunts get none (tap-only, weakest fighters); only the gang's lieutenants and captain fight with a held ability, and only the captain gets both slots filled.

trinketLoadout._comment: Enemy trinkets are rolled once per generated humanoid, from the same TrinketSystem catalog and base 8-point budget as players. Only effects supported by the shared ResourceSystem or bandit hit path are eligible. No new rigs, AI scans, guaranteed loot, or independent stat copies.

statWeakenMultiplierByRank._comment: Applied to attackDamage/maxHealth relative to the tier-scaled captain baseline -- 'their abilities are weakened for all except their camp's bandit captain'. Grunts in particular should read as genuinely weak fodder next to a captain, not just a smaller version of the same fighter.

difficultyTiers._comment: Eight danger tiers (0-7), one per 12 tiles from the wilderness entrance. Every tier adds modest stats; every TWO tiers improves the mastery and weapon-grade bands. Higher danger is driven primarily by better gear/abilities, not huge health inflation. Existing camp rank roles and loot tables stay unchanged.

combatPursuit._comment: Ordinary bandits pursue faster than the starting player's run, rather than standing on distant waiting rings. Movement still passes through the existing terrain/armor/debuff and player collision systems. Mine Ghouls/special non-bandit callers retain their own stat curves.

quickAttackTuning._comment: Only an equipped Quick Attack's own bonus condition enables it. Exhaust Cutter / Mercy Spike select more often with difficulty tier; Backstab Flick instead attempts tactical flanking and fires when behind. Flank and pursuit behavior preserves the existing two active melee slots.

campLifecycle._comment: How many simultaneous camps a wilderness zone with bandit_camp locales can host, and camp-clearing state used by docs/js/temporary-locales.js release()/re-stamp.

statMultiplierByRankAndTier._comment: Existing attack damage and Stamina scaling for each bandit rank and tier. Weak humanoids use separate healthMultiplierByRankAndTier for durability, so increasing their HP does not also increase their damage or attack budget.

healthMultiplierByRankAndTier._comment: Health-only rank curves for ordinary humanoids. Grunts survive a basic starting combo; lieutenants and flaskers remain tougher without raising their attack damage or Stamina. Captains fall back to statMultiplierByRankAndTier unchanged. The legacy Ghoul mine curves always take precedence.

flasker._comment: Flaskers roll two distinct authored throwable alchemy recipes once at spawn. AI throws do not consume this loadout; corpse loot guarantees several of the same two types.

legacyMineRankMultipliersByRank._comment: Original four wilderness danger rank curves, retained ONLY for Ghouls in the ten-band mine. The original tierStatBonus of 0.12 per floor band remains; eight new bandit tiers must not alter the deep mine's authored combat.
